bib.title: Revisiting the Calibration of Modern Neural Networks

legacy_report:
SOURCE: Revisiting the Calibration of Modern Neural Networks. Minderer, Djolonga, Romijnders, Hubis, Zhai, Houlsby, Tran, Lucic (Google Research, Brain Team). NeurIPS 2021, arXiv:2106.07998v2.

COVERAGE: 86,790 of 86,790 chars, all 28 pages. Nothing skipped; references skimmed. Figures were read from captions and extracted text only, not inspected as images.

CLAIMS
- claim: Recent families combine high accuracy with good calibration, so there is no general trend for recent or accurate networks to be poorly calibrated.
  number: none
  setup: ImageNet validation, unscaled and temperature-scaled. Holds for MLP-Mixer and ViT, and for BiT, which is convolutional. CLIP is well calibrated "given its accuracy".
  quote: "there is no general trend for recent or highly accurate neural networks to be poorly calibrated compared to older or less accurate models"
  where: p10
- claim: The released dataset covers far more models than the appendix table lists.
  number: 180 models, 16 families, 79 datasets, 28 metric variants
  setup: Released measurements. Table 1 has 28 rows across 8 families; the main text lists 7 families.
  quote: "comprising 180 distinct models from 16 families, each evaluated on 79 ImageNet-scale datasets and 28 metric variants"
  where: p2, p15
- claim: The default metric is top-label ECE with equal-mass bins.
  number: 100 bins
  setup: All main results. Appendices E and F repeat them with other ECE variants, NLL and Brier.
  quote: "we estimate ECE using equal-mass binning and 100 bins"
  where: p5
- claim: Temperature is fitted on a held-out part of clean validation data.
  number: 20% (10,000 images); evaluation on 40,000
  setup: ImageNet. ImageNet-C evaluation also excludes images derived from the held-out set.
  quote: "we reserve 20% of the IMAGE NET validation set (randomly sampled) for ﬁtting the temperature scaling parameter"
  where: p4, p15
- claim: Temperature scaling does not change accuracy, corrects average confidence, and exposes family differences that unscaled data hides.
  number: none
  setup: Single logit scale, fitted for likelihood.
  quote: "The classiﬁcation accuracy of the model is not affected by temperature scaling. A large fraction of model miscalibration is typically due to average over- or underconﬁdence"
  where: p3, p5
- claim: Under corruption, calibration error rises for all models once scaled, but more slowly for MLP-Mixer and ViT.
  number: 5 severities (15 perturbations, 75 datasets)
  setup: ImageNet-C, temperature fitted on clean ImageNet.
  quote: "this decay in calibration performance is slower for MLP-Mixer and ViT than for the other model families, both before and after temperature scaling"; "a consistent trend for higher calibration error under distribution shift for all models"
  where: p6, p21
- claim: Larger models are slightly worse calibrated in-distribution, but the trend reverses under shift for most families.
  number: none
  setup: ImageNet versus ImageNet-C, especially after scaling. ResNeXt-WSL is the in-distribution exception: larger models improve both accuracy and calibration.
  quote: "the trend is reversed for most model families as we move out of distribution"
  where: p2, p5 footnote 2, p6
- claim: A 300-fold increase in pretraining data leaves scaled ECE essentially unchanged.
  number: R50x1 ECE 0.0185, 0.0182, 0.0185; R101x3 ECE 0.0272, 0.0311, 0.0236
  setup: BiT only, pretrained on ImageNet (1.3M), ImageNet-21K (12.8M), JFT-300 (300M), then fine-tuned on ImageNet.
  quote: "the ECEs are 0.0185, 0.0182, 0.0185, respectively; for BiT-R101x3, they are 0.0272, 0.0311, 0.0236"
  where: p6
- claim: Longer pretraining makes a model more accurate and worse calibrated, moving it within its Pareto set.
  number: R101x3 error 0.176 vs 0.232; ECE 0.028 vs 0.019
  setup: BiT, pretraining step counts varied.
  quote: "for R101x3, 0.176 vs 0.232 in favor of the longer-trained model"; "for R101x3, 0.019 vs 0.028 in favor of the shorter-trained model"
  where: p6, p17
- claim: Architecture as the cause is inferred, not tested.
  number: none
  setup: Elimination of size and pretraining only.
  quote: "we speculate that model architecture, and in particular its spatial inductive bias, play an important role"
  where: p6
- claim: In selective prediction, the more accurate of two BiT models costs less at practical abstention rates.
  number: 0.08 error vs 0.009 ECE; up to 70%
  setup: BiT-R152x4 vs R50x1, ImageNet and ImageNet-R panels, cost ratio axis 1 to 100.
  quote: "(R152x4, by 0.08), and one with better ECE (R50x1, by 0.009). For abstention rates up to 70%"
  where: p8
- claim: The same preference holds in other pairs, including one with equal gaps.
  number: ViT 0.076 error vs 0.007 ECE; ViT-B/32 vs ResNeXt-WSL 32d, 0.03 vs 0.03
  setup: Same cost model, Appendix B.3. Exceptions occur only "in a few cases and at very high abstention rates".
  quote: "0.076 lower classiﬁcation error (0.194 vs. 0.118) and 0.007 higher ECE (0.017 vs. 0.01)"; "has 0.03 lower (better) classiﬁcation error while the ViT model has 0.03 lower (better) ECE"
  where: p17, p18
- claim: ECE estimators have opposing biases, so the bin count can flip the sign of the ECE-accuracy relationship.
  number: 15 bins (2667 points/bin), 100 (400), 5000 (8)
  setup: Temperature-scaled BiT models on ImageNet. Binning bias is negative; finite-sample bias is positive and depends on accuracy.
  quote: "whether this relationship is positive or negative depends on the number of bins used for estimating ECE"
  where: p9, p10
- claim: Models that are Pareto-optimal on ImageNet stay so on natural OOD sets, so joint comparison resolves most rank flips between ECE variants.
  number: none
  setup: ImageNetV2, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-A; ECE variants, NLL, Brier.
  quote: "the Pareto-optimal models rarely change, even if the ranking based on ECE alone does"
  where: p7, p10
- claim: Label smoothing produces underconfidence rather than better intrinsic calibration; train without it and rescale afterwards.
  number: none
  setup: EfficientNet-B4 on ImageNet and ImageNet-C. The authors say ResNets behave similarly.
  quote: "models should be trained without label smoothing and then recalibrated by temperature scaling post hoc"
  where: p21

LIMITS
- Covers image classification at ImageNet scale only; the models date from 2021 or earlier.
- The authors concede ECE estimation is biased, and that "real-world cost structures are complex and may yield different results".
- Generalisation is left open: "Further work ... will be necessary to tell whether these results generalize".
- The study does not compare calibration methods beyond temperature scaling.
- Size and pretraining are the only explanations tested, and the pretraining test uses BiT only.
- The paper does not say whether the ECE gaps in the cost analysis are scaled or unscaled.
- Author overlap: Minderer, Zhai, Houlsby and Lucic also appear on the printed references for some top families (ViT, MLP-Mixer, BiT). The paper declares no competing interests and does not discuss this.

BUILDS ON: Guo et al. 2017 (temperature scaling, the trend under test); Naeini et al. 2015 (ECE); Nixon et al. 2019 and Roelofs et al. 2020 (ECE variants and bias); Kumar et al. 2019 (binning bias, top-label); Bröcker 2009 (definition); Ovadia et al. 2019 (calibration under shift); Hendrycks & Dietterich 2019 (ImageNet-C); Brier 1950; DeGroot & Fienberg 1983; Hernández-Orallo et al. 2012 (cost); Djolonga et al. 2020 (Robustness Metrics).

CODE: None in the PDF. Repository: https://github.com/google-research/robustness_metrics/tree/master/robustness_metrics/projects/revisiting_calibration (p2 footnote).

FIGURES
- Fig 2, p5, "Temperature scaling reveals consistent properties of model families": shows families overlapping before scaling and separating after.
- Fig 4, p7, ImageNet-C before and after scaling: shows decay by family in one view.
- Fig 7, p8, selective prediction relative cost: shows where accuracy beats calibration.
- Fig 9, p10, "The effect of binning-induced bias in ECE depends on accuracy": shows the sign flip faster than prose.
- Fig 19/20, pp27-28, reliability diagrams for all models: would link to the note's reliability-diagram section.

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions.
- Extraction: plot axis labels appear as stray text, equations 3 and 5 are partly garbled, and small caps split as "IMAGE NET". Quotes join line breaks and keep the ligatures.
- Inconsistencies in the source:
  - Temperature holdout is "a held-out portion of the training data" on p3 but the validation set on p4.
  - ImageNet-21K is 12.8M images on p6 but 14.2M on p16.
  - Fig 12 text says "eight model pairs", but the labels show nine and panels run (a) to (i), so the text's panel letters do not line up.
  - The Lemma 1 bias has (1−δi), the derivation (1−2δi).
  - Fig 7 and p8 contain the typo "with better with better".
- The direction of the Fig 9 flip at each bin count was not read, because it is only visible in the image.

COMPARISON WITH data-science/01-classical-ml/notes/04-model-evaluation.md (lines 402-412)

No numeric mismatch. These all match the source: 180 models and 16 families; 0.08 vs 0.009; 70%; clean-ImageNet fit; slower decay for Mixer and ViT; "every family" (p21, though p6 says "generally"); "only speculate" (p6). The Guo sentences on line 404 (CIFAR-100, LeNet, ResNet-110, depth and width) cannot be checked from this source and were not audited. This paper quotes Guo only on the general trend.

Framing or inference, not supported as written:
1. Line 406, "Three of their limits". The paper's "Pitfalls and Limitations" section (section 5) is only about ECE estimation, which covers only the bin-count half of the third bullet. The first two bullets and the cost result are findings, not limits the authors concede.
2. Line 409, "a temperature fitted before shift doesn't fully carry over". This is the note's inference, and the paper never states it. The paper's framing leans the other way:
   - "modern image models are well calibrated across distribution shifts" (p10)
   - larger, accurate models "can maintain their good in-distribution calibration even under severe distribution shifts" (p7)
   - "changes in ECE are much smaller than changes in classiﬁcation error" (Fig 5)
   The inference is defensible, but as written it reads as the authors' point. It should be marked as the note's reading or paired with the authors' framing.

Under-qualified or missing setup:
3. Line 404, "among the best calibrated" has no setup. Missing: top-label ECE, equal-mass, 100 bins, ImageNet validation. Unscaled, BiT (convolutional) overlaps Mixer and ViT (p5), so the non-convolutional separation is clearer after scaling.
4. Line 404, "Size and pretraining don't fully explain the gap". The pretraining evidence is BiT only. The size claim has an exception, ResNeXt-WSL (footnote 2). "Only speculate" is accurate for p6, but the abstract and conclusion say "major determinant", so the note is more cautious than the paper's headline. A reader checking the abstract will see the difference.
5. Line 410, the cost result is given for one pair, which understates it and leaves a gap:
   - The paper says "The same is true for all other model families we study".
   - The 0.08 vs 0.009 gap is lopsided, so a reader may assume it drives the result. The 0.03 vs 0.03 pair, where accuracy still wins in "most practical cost settings", answers that and is omitted.
   - The 70% figure belongs to the R152x4/R50x1 pair. ImageNet and ImageNet-R and the cost ratio range of 1 to 100 are not stated.
   - The comparison is mainly within a family's Pareto set (p7). Across families the paper says the Pareto sets establish "a clear preference".
6. Line 410, bin count. Missing setup: temperature-scaled BiT on ImageNet, 15/100/5000 bins, with 5000 being only 8 points per bin. The paper says this is especially a problem "when comparing models with widely varying accuracies". The remedy is also partial: the paper adds "a careful choice of bin size" and offers Brier and NLL as alternatives. The note's own demo already uses Brier.
7. Line 410 uses "ECE" and "BiT" with no definition. A case-sensitive search finds both only on this line, so "ECE" is never expanded in the note.
8. Line 402, "Often overconfident" is broadly consistent with "most models are slightly overconfident in-distribution" (p20). However, EfficientNet-NS is underconfident, and the paper attributes this possibly to label smoothing.
9. Line 404, "180 models from 16 families" is correctly worded as a release. A reader could still assume the reported findings rest on all 180; Table 1 lists 28 rows.

Omitted findings the caller may want:
- The headline itself is not stated: no general trend to poor calibration, and accuracy and calibration are not in simple conflict. Line 404 implies it, and the references row says "qualify Guo's finding", but the note never says what is qualified.
- Larger models are more robust under shift, reversing the in-distribution trend.
- Pareto-optimal models stay so on natural OOD sets. Line 409 covers only synthetic corruption.
- Label smoothing confounds calibration comparisons.
- The fit used a 20% holdout (10,000 images).
